How to read it

The teacher is a large video model. For every frame it writes a 256-number description of the scene. The student is a recurrent network whose only recurrent connections are the 91,663 real synapses between these neurons, with their real excitatory or inhibitory signs. It receives a 64×64 glimpse into the visual neurons and the movement command into the compass and motor groups, and is trained to reproduce the teacher's numbers. Nothing else is given.

When the picture is removed (steps 9 to 16) the visual group goes quiet and the central complex keeps working. The match falls but the brain keeps predicting the teacher from its own motion. When the picture returns the match recovers.

Times Square is hard: one seed, 120 training episodes, a narrow view and real clutter, so the match is lower than in the synthetic arena and can drop to zero late in a walk. Across the test set the real wiring still predicts best (blind error 0.885 vs 0.906 scrambled, 0.917 random, 0.907 GRU).
